Cathie Wood Says AI Could Cut Drug Costs by $1.8 Billion. These 5 ARK-Backed Biotech Stocks Could Benefit
desc:
The biggest payoff from artificial intelligence may not come from making software smarter. It could come from making medicine dramatically cheaper to develop. Cathie Wood believes AI and sequencing technology could cut the cost of bringing a new drug to market by as much as $1.8 billion — while giving pharmaceutical companies years of additional patent-protected sales.

A $1.8 Billion Opportunity

Speaking to WOLF Financial on Nov. 18, the ARK Invest founder said developing a new drug currently costs about $2.4 billion and takes 13 years, including the cost of failed clinical trials.

"With AI and sequencing technologies," Wood said, ARK believes that within five years the cost could fall to $600 million-$700 million, while development time could shrink to eight years or fewer.

That implies potential savings of $1.7 billion-$1.8 billion per drug. The time savings could be just as valuable: Drugs typically carry 20-plus years of patent protection, and reaching the market sooner could give companies more years to generate revenue before generic competition arrives.

Wood also cautioned that the gains will not be shared equally. "Some companies are going to do this well and some companies are not," she said, warning that businesses that fail to adapt could lose ground as patents expire.

Read Also: Nvidia GPUs Alone Won't Win AI Drug Discovery

Five Stocks in ARK’s Portfolio

ARK’s third-quarter 2026 portfolio disclosures show positions in five companies spanning AI-led drug discovery and genetic medicine.

Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ:RXRX) uses its AI-native Recursion OS to connect biological data, machine learning and laboratory experiments. ARK held a position worth about $184.8 million, or 1.06% of its reported portfolio, at Sept. 30, according to Q3 holdings data.

Absci Corp. (NASDAQ:ABSI) combines generative AI with laboratory validation to design antibody-based medicines. Its platform aims to move from AI-designed antibodies to lab-validated candidates in as little as six weeks, according to the company. ARK’s position represented 0.74% of its portfolio.

CRISPR Therapeutics (NASDAQ:CRSP) is developing gene-editing treatments, including its approved Casgevy therapy and a broader pipeline of genetic medicines. It was the largest of these five positions at 3.2% of ARK’s portfolio.

Intellia Therapeutics (NASDAQ:NTLA) is advancing CRISPR-based treatments designed to address the underlying causes of serious diseases. Its late-stage pipeline includes candidates for hereditary angioedema and transthyretin amyloidosis. The position represented 1.11% of ARK’s portfolio.

Beam Therapeutics (NASDAQ:BEAM) uses base editing, a gene-editing approach designed to make precise changes to individual DNA letters. Its pipeline includes candidates for sickle cell disease and genetic disorders. ARK’s position accounted for 1.66% of its portfolio.

Investment Takeaway

Wood’s forecast is a technology-driven opportunity, not a guarantee of lower costs or faster approvals. Clinical failures, regulatory hurdles, manufacturing and financing needs remain significant risks, particularly for early-stage biotech companies. Investors should also remember that ARK’s disclosed holdings reflect positions as of Sept. 30, not a promise to keep owning these stocks.

The bigger question is which companies can turn AI and sequencing advances into successful medicines — and capture the commercial value of getting them to patients sooner.

Read Also: AI Could Make Biology Programmable, Expert Says

Buy Now, Pay Later Is Becoming a Holiday Shopping Lifeline. Should Affirm Investors Be Excited?
desc:
The biggest holiday shopping trend may not be what Americans are buying, but how they are paying for it. Buy now, pay later (BNPL) is becoming a bigger part of the checkout experience as consumers look to spread expenses across paychecks. For Affirm Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:AFRM), that could mean a bigger holiday opportunity — but rising usage is not automatically a sign of stronger consumer finances.

A $21 Billion Holiday Opportunity

Adobe expects U.S. consumers to spend a record $21.3 billion through BNPL during November and December 2026, up 6.6% year over year. That is part of a broader $275.1 billion online holiday shopping forecast.

The payment method is expected to account for $1.09 billion in online purchases on Cyber Monday alone, with another $807 million on Black Friday. Mobile devices will drive 82% of BNPL spending, highlighting how closely installment payments are tied to online shopping and quick checkout decisions. news.adobe.com+1

The opportunity extends beyond younger shoppers or households with limited access to credit. A Nov. 23 Reuters report on Block, Inc. (NYSE:XYZ) consumer research found that 69% of deferred-payment users in households earning at least $100,000 had used BNPL or checkout financing over the past year, compared with 61% of users earning under $50,000.

But the findings also reveal the other side of the trend: 72% of respondents said they had financed a purchase because paying the entire amount upfront would have felt financially stressful, even though they had the money.

Read Also: Buy-Now-Pay-Later Is Moving Into Essential Services, Not Just Retail

Affirm Has More Than Holiday Momentum

Affirm’s latest results suggest the company is entering the holiday season with considerable momentum. In its fiscal first-quarter 2027 results, gross merchandise volume (GMV) — the total value of transactions processed on its platform — jumped 34% year over year to $14.4 billion. Revenue climbed 35% to $1.26 billion, while active consumers increased 19% to 28.7 million.

Its direct-to-consumer business is also gaining traction. Affirm Card GMV surged 117% to $3.3 billion, accounting for 23% of the company’s total GMV during the quarter. That gives Affirm another route to reach consumers beyond merchant checkout partnerships.

But the opportunity is not exclusive to Affirm. PayPal Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:PYPL) and Block, Inc. (NYSE:XYZ) are also competing for installment-payment transactions, while private player Klarna remains a significant rival. More consumer adoption does not guarantee that Affirm will capture a disproportionate share of the growth.

The Credit Risk Investors Cannot Ignore

There is another number worth watching. Affirm’s allowance for credit losses rose to 6.3% of loans held for investment in September, compared with 5.9% a year earlier. That does not establish a deterioration in repayment performance, but it highlights why investors should look beyond transaction growth.

Investment Takeaway: Affirm has a compelling holiday growth opportunity, supported by expanding consumer adoption and strong transaction momentum. But the real test for investors will come after the shopping season: whether higher volumes translate into sustainable revenue without a disproportionate increase in credit losses.

Adobe’s $21.3 billion forecast is encouraging for the industry; Affirm’s ability to convert that demand into profitable growth is what ultimately matters.

title: Inflation May Have Peaked in October: Economists Split on How Many Fed Hikes Are Effectively Needed
desc:
A Federal Reserve inflation tracker is flashing a zero for November.

The Cleveland Fed’s inflation nowcast, a daily model built on oil and gasoline prices, estimates that US consumer prices were unchanged in November from October.

That would be the softest monthly reading since June, when the consumer price index fell 0.4%.

So is US inflation finally near its peak?

Gasoline explains most of the relief. The national average for regular gas has slipped below $3.60 a gallon, down from nearly $4.50 in late September, according to the American Automobile Association.

The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, rose 3.8% from a year earlier in October, the Bureau of Economic Analysis said Wednesday.

“Recent declines in gasoline prices suggest that headline PCE inflation may have peaked,” HSBC economist Ryan Wang said in a note Wednesday.

Wang expects one final quarter-point hike in December, lifting the federal funds target range to 4.00%-4.25%, and then no change through 2027.

Not every economist agrees that one hike will be enough.

The same report carried a warning. Core PCE, which strips out food and energy, rose 0.3% for a third straight month and climbed to 3.3% year over year, a new high for 2026.

Read Also: Fed's Preferred Inflation Gauge Hits 3.8% as Expected: Q3 GDP Growth Revised Up to 4.3% (UPDATED)

Wall Street has seen this movie before.

The 2022 Lesson: Headline Inflation Peaks First

In June 2022, headline PCE inflation topped out at 7.2%, according to Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis data.

Gasoline prices were already rolling over. However, core inflation kept rising and reached 5.6% in September 2022, three months after the headline peak.

As a result, the Fed did not stop. The upper bound of its policy rate stood at 1.75% at the end of June 2022. By July 2023, it was 5.50%.

That is 375 basis points of tightening after inflation had already peaked.

Core Inflation Is Still Climbing

The same split is showing up in real time.

The same Cleveland Fed nowcast puts November headline PCE at 3.78%, slightly below October’s 3.84%. Meanwhile, it sees core PCE rising further to 3.38%.

Pantheon Macroeconomics chief US economist Samuel Tombs expects core PCE to peak at 3.4% in November before easing to 3.0% by May 2027.

Still, he does not see energy as the only culprit. “The breadth of momentum in services prices points to some demand-driven inflation too,” Tombs said.

Barclays and 22V Research Expect More From the Fed

Barclays economist Pooja Sriram sees two more quarter-point hikes, one in December and another in January.

On a three-month annualized basis, core PCE accelerated to 3.6% in October, the same pace last seen in April, according to Barclays. The data “do not offer evidence that inflation is returning to target at sufficient speed,” Sriram said.

The economy is not helping. Third-quarter gross domestic product growth was revised up to 4.3% from 3.5%, driven by consumer spending and business investment.

For Peter Williams of 22V Research, that speed is the problem. Nominal growth of roughly 6.3% is “simply too strong to be durably consistent with inflation returning to target,” Williams said.

Read Also: S&P 500 Pares Losses as Fed Beige Book Signals Optimism: 10 Tech Stocks Bouncing off Lows on Wednesday

Bonds Bet on the Peak

Treasuries rallied on Wednesday. The 10-year yield fell 6.4 basis points to 4.86%, while the 2-year yield dropped 3.7 basis points to 4.65%. The 30-year yield slid 6.5 basis points to 5.25%.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (NASDAQ:TLT) gained 0.9%, and the iShares TIPS Bond ETF (NYSE:TIP) rose 0.4%.

Not everyone sees core inflation heading higher. Truflation, which tracks prices in real time, forecasts November headline and core PCE at 3.7% and 3.2%, respectively.

The next PCE report lands on Dec. 23, two weeks after the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.

By then, the gas station may have delivered its relief. Whether core prices follow will decide if December’s hike is the last one, or just the first after the peak.

title: Stock Valuations Just Fell to 2018 Levels: Last Time, the Recession Never Came
desc:
Stock investors are bracing for a recession. The economy has not received the memo.

Valuation multiples on the major U.S. stock indexes have dropped in recent weeks to levels last seen during the 2018 correction and the 2020 bear market, according to Yardeni Research. Over the same weeks, the government said the economy grew at a 4.3% annualized pace in the third quarter.

That gap is now the central question for Wall Street heading into December.

The Market Is Pricing a Downturn

The S&P 500 closed at 7,182.78 on Wednesday, 8.1% below its record close of 7,818.93 on Oct. 6. At its Nov. 20 close, the index was down 11.6% from that peak, deep in correction territory.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) has lost 6% over the past month.

For Yardeni Research president Ed Yardeni, the falling multiples carry a clear message about what investors fear.

“They are clearly worried that analysts’ consensus earnings expectations are irrationally exuberant,” Yardeni said in a note Wednesday. In other words, investors suspect that the AI buildout that has powered the economy could now tip it into a recession.

Sentiment has turned just as fast. The Investors Intelligence Bull/Bear Ratio, which compares bullish and bearish investment newsletters, peaked at 3.88 in the week of Aug. 17. Last week, it fell to 1.13.

“From a contrarian perspective, that’s a very bullish reading,” Yardeni said.

Read Also: Big Tech Just Became a Value Trade — Something Wall Street Hasn't Seen in 20 Years

The Data Say Otherwise

The economic numbers point the other way.

Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to an annualized 4.3% on Wednesday, from 3.4% in the first estimate, according to Deutsche Bank. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, a measure some economists call “core GDP,” rose 5.8%.

Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 in the week ended Nov. 21, below the 200,000 economists expected. New home sales jumped to an annualized 701,000, the highest this year.

Deutsche Bank strategist Jim Reid said in a note Thursday that “the US macro data has remained incredibly positive,” adding that “there was still no sign of a broader macro slowdown that’s driven many past selloffs.”

December 2018: The Recession That Never Showed Up

The closest parallel may be the fall of 2018.

Back then, the Federal Reserve was raising interest rates into a strong economy, and investors feared it would go too far. The S&P 500 fell 19.8% from Sept. 20 to Dec. 24, 2018, stopping just short of a bear market. The Fed raised rates again on Dec. 19.

The recession never came. The index recovered its September high by April 23, 2019, and was up 37.1% a year after the Christmas Eve low.

The setup today rhymes. The Fed is again raising rates into strength, with a policy rate of 4% and markets pricing another hike at the Dec. 9 meeting. Core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred gauge, rose 3.3% from a year earlier in October, above forecasts.

“We expect a similar outcome this time, and that the current correction won’t turn into a bear market,” Yardeni said. He sees the selloff as the post-midterms buying opportunity he first flagged on Sept. 15.

Read Also: 3 Things Every Bear Market in 50 Years Had in Common — Which One Is Missing Now?

Why History Might Not Repeat

Not everyone is ready to call the bottom.

Yardeni himself flagged the risk in the sentiment data. The Bull/Bear ratio “has fallen below 1.00 and stayed there for a few weeks during bear markets and long corrections,” he said.

Reid offered a sharper warning from the dot-com era.

“Even after the dot com bubble, remember that the S&P 500 only entered bear market territory in March 2001, a full year after the peak, just as the US was entering an outright recession,” he said.

In other words, a strong economy today does not rule out a weaker one tomorrow. It only means the stock market is moving first.

The question now is which side blinks: the investors pricing a downturn, or the data that refuse to show one.

title: Walmart, McDonald's Are Rallying: GLP-1 Drugs Say the Food Trade Won't Last
desc:
Thanksgiving is the one day of the year when Americans are expected to overeat.

For a fast-growing slice of the country, a weekly shot or a daily pill is now quietly saying no.

Oxford Economics expects the number of Americans taking GLP-1 drugs, the appetite-suppressing medicines behind Wegovy, Ozempic and Zepbound, to nearly double to 60 million by 2030.

Adoption is running ahead of the firm’s earlier forecasts.

“We estimate the average GLP-1-using household reduces spending on food by close to $500 per year, and increases spending on apparel by $200,” Oxford Economics U.S. economist Grace Zwemmer, the report’s author, said this week.

According to Zwemmer, groceries and spending at bars and restaurants are the categories most at risk.

Wall Street is betting the other way.

The Stocks That Should Be Worried Are Rallying

Since the end of September, Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) has climbed 27%, and McDonald’s Corp. (NYSE:MCD) has gained 22.8%. Costco Wholesale Corp. (NASDAQ:COST) is up 19.4%.

Snack makers have joined in. Mondelez International Inc. (NASDAQ:MDLZ) has rallied 17.3%, Hershey Co. (NYSE:HSY) 15.8% and General Mills Inc. (NYSE:GIS) 12.7%.

In other words, the companies selling the food that GLP-1 users skip are among the market’s best performers this fall.

The Biggest Flight To Staples Since The Fund’s Launch

The Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (NYSE:XLP) has gained 14.5% since Sept. 30, through Wednesday’s close. Over the same stretch, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) has lost 6%, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) has dropped 14.3%.

Measured against SPY, XLP has outperformed by 21.9% over October and November, with two sessions left in the month. That is the strongest two-month run of relative performance, measured from month-end, since the fund launched in December 1998.

The previous record came in October and November 2000, when the ratio rose 20.1% as the dot-com bubble deflated.

Then, as now, the move said more about what investors were selling than about what they were buying. Money left technology in search of cash flows that do not depend on the next round of AI spending.

That exit has been violent this time. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down about 40% from its June record, and Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) has lost 29.9% in a month.

Read Also: QUICK SPARK: Nasdaq 100 Index Is Heading for Its Worst 2-Month Drop Since 2008

Staples, in short, are being bought as shelter, not as food companies.

Why Oxford’s Numbers Still Matter

Total U.S. GLP-1 prescriptions reached 12.91 million in October, up 30.5% from a year earlier, according to IQVIA data compiled by Jefferies. Oral versions have climbed to 10.5% of prescriptions from 2.4% a year ago.

The data “continues to support an expansion rather than cannibalization framework,” Jefferies analyst David Windley said in a note last week.

Food companies have faced a diet scare before. On May 7, 2004, Krispy Kreme Doughnuts Inc. issued its first profit warning since going public in 2000, blaming the Atkins and South Beach low-carb diets. By mid-2005, the share of adults on a low-carb diet had fallen to 2% from 9% at the peak, according to NPD Group, and the fad was over.

That flips the script. A diet asks people to ignore the hunger signal. A GLP-1 turns down the volume of the signal itself, and prescriptions get refilled long after willpower fades.

Even within staples, the pure food trade is lagging. The Invesco Food & Beverage ETF (NYSE:PBJ) has gained only 4.8% since Sept. 30, a third of XLP’s advance.

How GLP-1 Exposed Stocks Have Traded Since Sept. 30

Read Also: 3 Things Every Bear Market in 50 Years Had in Common — Which One Is Missing Now?

The Bill Lands In Washington, Too

Oxford estimates the net federal cost of GLP-1s will reach $18 billion in 2034, adding 0.9% to the deficit.

“Medicare coverage and longer lifespans will push up Medicare and Social Security costs, which lower healthcare needs and higher tax contributions will only partly offset,” Zwemmer added.

Rotations end when the fear that drives them fades.

When money starts flowing back into technology, staples will be judged again on what they sell. Oxford’s research suggests that, for a growing number of households, the answer is less food.

title: Mark Cuban Says He’d ‘Love Universal Healthcare’ at Just $10 a Month for Every American — ‘Even the Most Libertarian Person Would Say Yes’
desc:
Ten dollars a month would settle America’s universal healthcare fight in a hurry. The catch is that nobody can see what the system actually costs.

Cost Plus Drugs co-founder Mark Cuban likes the idea of covering everyone. He just doesn’t think anyone can put an honest price on it yet.

"I would love universal healthcare," Cuban said on "The Prof G Pod" on Nov. 16. "I mean, if all of a sudden we came up with new ways to do things and it was $10 per person per month and everybody got coverage, everybody, even the most libertarian person would say yes."

"The problem is we don’t have access to all that information," he continued.

Cuban was answering a listener who asked how health coverage keeps people stuck in corporate jobs when they’d rather start a business. He told the listener there’s no quick fix.

Nobody Can Read The Bill

In Cuban’s view, the universal healthcare debate stalls because neither patients nor employers can see what care really costs, and the government is in the dark too.

That blind spot lands hardest on employers. About 71% of covered workers are now in self-funded plans, where the employer pays medical claims out of its own pocket instead of buying insurance, according to KFF’s 2026 Employer Health Benefits Survey.

Cuban urged those employers to run their benefits contracts through AI tools and ask where they’re getting overcharged. He also called the biggest vertically integrated players "too big to care."

A Bill That Never Retires

Cuban described insurance premiums as the "one debt you have to pay for the rest of your life."

"Even when you hit 65 and you go on Medicare, you’re still writing checks till the day you die," he said.

The checks keep getting bigger. The average annual premium for employer-sponsored family coverage reached $28,303 in 2026, up 5% from 2025, according to KFF. That outpaced 3.7% wage growth and 2.7% inflation.

Workers’ own share of family coverage climbed 9% to $7,471 a year, KFF found.

Spread across 12 months, that total family premium works out to about $2,359 a month. Cuban’s hypothetical runs $10 per person.

Transparency Before Politics

Cuban has been trying to prove that sunlight drives prices down since launching Cost Plus Drugs in 2022. The online pharmacy posts its pricing publicly and sells medications at cost plus a 15% markup.

His argument on the podcast followed the same logic. A universal system built without real cost and claims data would be negotiated blind, whether it’s single-payer or something else entirely.

That’s why he treats transparency as the first step rather than a side issue. In his telling, every promise about what universal coverage would cost is a guess until the contracts are public.

A $10 health plan sounds like something pitched on late-night TV. Cuban’s point is that America can’t tell how far reality sits from that number until somebody opens the books.

title: Walmart Is Winning Thanksgiving. Is Target Losing the Holiday Shopping Battle?
desc:
Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) is making Thanksgiving dinner a $3.50-per-person proposition. Target Corp (NYSE:TGT) is offering a $5-per-person meal. That gap captures a fight among retailers: winning shoppers watching every dollar without giving up holiday traditions that bring them into stores.

Walmart’s $35 meal for 10 is down from $39.93 last year and includes 18% more individual items, according to Axios. Target is advertising a $30 meal for six, keeping its price unchanged for a second year, according to NBC News. On a per-person basis, Walmart’s offer is 30% cheaper.

Walmart Makes Value the Main Event

Thanksgiving baskets are more than seasonal promotions. They are a visible test of how far a retailer can stretch a household’s budget — and a reason to choose one store for the rest of the shopping list.

Walmart is leaning into that proposition with a one-click basket built around a turkey, sides and pumpkin pie. Aldi is advertising a meal for 10 for under $39, although its basket has fewer items than last year’s.

Costco Wholesale Corp (NASDAQ:COST) is taking a different tack: its prepared Thanksgiving dinner costs $199.99 for eight, unchanged from 2025, and is positioned as a ready-to-serve option.

Kroger Co (NYSE:KR) has moved away from a fixed-price meal bundle, instead promoting individual discounts and prepared foods in different portion sizes.

That leaves Walmart competing on price, convenience and the perception of getting more for less.

The Margin Trade-Off

There is a catch for investors. Retailers may sacrifice profit on holiday staples to get shoppers through the door, hoping they add snacks, drinks and other groceries to their carts.

Wholesale frozen turkey prices were up 12% year over year as of Nov. 9, reported Reuters, while wholesale russet potato prices had climbed about 46%. Retailers have kept consumer prices comparatively restrained, absorbing some pressure to reinforce their value message.

Read Also: Grocers Keep Thanksgiving Meals Cheap as Turkey Costs Rise

Walmart’s scale and grocery reach make its aggressive pricing important to watch. Target’s offer is cheaper in total dollars, but serves fewer people; Costco is selling convenience rather than the lowest cost per guest. Kroger’s flexible approach may appeal to shoppers who want to build their own meal.

Why it Matters

One Thanksgiving promotion cannot determine which retailer is winning the holiday season. But the offers show how differently these chains are positioning themselves as affordability remains a consumer concern.

Investors should watch comparable-sales results, grocery traffic and management commentary on promotions and margins. If Walmart’s basket brings shoppers back for more than turkey, it could strengthen its competitive position. For Target, the test is whether its value offer translates into broader store traffic — not simply whether it can match Walmart’s price per person.

title: Intel Stock Is on the Verge of a Death Cross. Is Its Comeback Already in Trouble?
desc:
Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC) has some signs that its comeback is gaining traction: data-center revenue is surging, an outside customer has signed on for its advanced manufacturing process, and Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT) has chosen its packaging technology for Azure chips.

Yet the stock is telling a different story. A bearish technical signal is just cents away, putting the market’s faith in the turnaround under scrutiny.

A Death Cross Is Near

Chart created using Benzinga Pro

Intel shares trade around $54.47, below their eight-day and 20-day moving averages of $55.15 and $59.36. More importantly, the 50-day average is $87.70, barely above the 200-day average at $87.66. The four-cent gap puts the stock on the verge of a Death Cross, which occurs when the 50-day average falls below the 200-day.

The setup reflects Intel’s recent decline, but it is not confirmation yet. The 14-day relative strength index is 35.93, signaling weakness without reaching the conventional oversold threshold of 30. The MACD (moving average convergence/divergence) indicator remains below zero, although its positive histogram reading of 1.15 suggests selling momentum may be easing. A rebound could still delay the crossover.

Read Also: Intel Just Took 14A Off Death Row — The 2028 Clock Is Ticking

The Comeback Has Real Progress

There are reasons investors might resist writing off the recovery. Third-quarter revenue rose 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, while Data Center and AI revenue grew 78% to $7.32 billion. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said demand for Intel CPUs remains robust and called Xeon demand "extraordinary," while identifying additional supply as an immediate priority.

Intel also secured its first external customer for its 18A-P manufacturing process, although it has not disclosed the customer’s identity.

Separately, Microsoft became the first publicly named customer for Intel Foundry’s EMIB packaging technology for Azure silicon, alongside a multiyear Xeon supply agreement. These are meaningful endorsements, but not yet proof of a profitable foundry business at scale.

The Market Still Wants Proof

The counterweight is Intel’s uneven outlook. Client Computing revenue fell 5% to $8.1 billion in the third quarter, and management expects the PC slowdown to persist through at least the first half of 2027.

Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion. Its foundry segment also posted a $1.9 billion operating loss, while external revenue was only $411 million.

Investment Takeaway

The approaching Death Cross does not prove Intel’s turnaround has failed; moving averages are lagging indicators, and the MACD histogram hints that selling pressure could be cooling.

But the chart captures the burden facing Tan: turn customer wins and AI demand into consistent shipments, stronger foundry economics and better guidance. Until investors see that, good news may struggle to repair confidence.

title: Bitcoin Needs to Return to 'Original Narrative' to Hit $100,000, Bloomberg Analyst Says
desc:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) reclaiming $100,000 could reinforce its reputation as a resilient asset and attract a fresh wave of investment from skeptical investors, according to Bloomberg Senior ETF analyst Eric Balchunas.

Speaking on CoinDesk’s Markets Outlook, Balchunas noted that a subsequent break above its all-time high could unlock another wave of institutional and retail demand.

Getting back to $100,000 remains the biggest challenge.

While portfolio managers and hedge funds could rotate capital into Bitcoin given its depressed valuation, sustained demand will require broader adoption.

Despite Bitcoin’s 50% drawdown, 91% of ETF investors have maintained exposure, with cumulative inflows nearing $60 billion.

Balchunas argued that ETF flows follow Bitcoin’s price rather than drive it, making broader demand key to recovery.

Bitcoin Is Experiencing Gold’s ‘Doghouse’ Era

Balchunas compared Bitcoin’s downturn to gold’s struggles between 2011 and 2019.

The SPDR Gold Trust (NYSE:GLD) reached $76 billion in assets in 2011, briefly becoming the world’s largest ETF, before taking eight years to reclaim that milestone.

Around half of its investors exited during that period. Gold subsequently rallied approximately 450% from its period of extreme pessimism, according to Balchunas.

He argued that assets without cash flows, such as Bitcoin and gold, can experience prolonged downturns before sentiment triggers explosive recoveries.

Is $55,000 Bitcoin’s Bottom?

Balchunas stopped short of calling $55,000 the definitive bottom but suggested that prices around that level could attract Bitcoin’s most committed investors.

He argued that Bitcoin must return to its original narrative of scarcity, inflation protection and censorship resistance rather than relying on ETF adoption or regulatory developments.

“Bitcoin needs to return to the original narrative,” Balchunas said.

title: S&P 500 Pares Losses as Fed Beige Book Signals Optimism: 10 Tech Stocks Bouncing off Lows on Wednesday
desc:
Wall Street went back to the scene of Friday’s panic on Wednesday. This time, the floor held, and the selloff lost its grip.

The Nasdaq 100 sank as low as 24,970.66 in the first half hour of trading. That was roughly 60 points above the 24,910.48 intraday low it hit on Friday, Nov. 20.

From there, the index climbed 3.9% to 25,951 by 2 p.m. ET, trimming its daily loss to 1%.

The S&P 500 traveled the same road. After falling as much as 3.2% to 6,970.11, it recovered to 7,174.52, down just 0.4%.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average swung more than 1,300 points from its low and turned higher, adding 230 points, or 0.5%, to 50,249. The Russell 2000 rose 0.9% to 2,709.

Read Also: Nasdaq 100 Drops 2.5% on AI Credit Fears, Nvidia Sinks 7%: Stock Market Today

What Broke at the Open

Three blows landed in the first hour. First, credit. Worries about the debt behind the artificial-intelligence buildout returned, with five-year credit-default swaps on CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) at 13.3%, up from 4.47% at their June lows, according to FactSet data. Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) fell as much as 9.1% before paring the drop to 4.5% at $148.35.

Second, trade. The U.S. Trade Representative proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including up to 20% on China, 15% on the European Union, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, 25% on India and 35% on Vietnam. Hearings start Jan. 25, 2027, so the duties are not immediate.

Third, inflation. Core PCE prices rose 3.3% from a year earlier in October, above the 3.2% forecast. At the same time, third-quarter GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized pace, well above the 3.5% estimate.

“The big highlight from this morning’s data is GDP, which at 4.3% shows that the economy is booming, but unfortunately the inflation data is still too high and is unlikely to convince the Fed to remain on hold,” Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer at Northlight Asset Management, said in emailed comments.

Why the Nasdaq 100 Retest Matters

Friday’s low was not a random number. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 5.6% that day, then surged 6.9% on Monday after Jensen Huang‘s return to Nvidia, before giving back 2% on Tuesday.

Wednesday was the first real test of that bottom. When an index returns to a recent low and bounces before breaking it, chart watchers call it a higher low, often an early sign that sellers are tiring.

The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) rose 4.3% from its morning low. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH) did better, climbing 6.8% off its trough.

Still, the Nasdaq 100 remains down 8.6% in November.

The Beige Book Brings a Steadier Read

The Federal Reserve’s Beige Book landed at 2 p.m. ET, with most of the rebound already in place, and did not derail it.

Eight of the 12 Fed districts reported slight to moderate growth, while four reported no change, a touch softer than October’s nine. However, the outlook was firmer. “Overall, the majority of Districts expected slight to moderate growth,” the report said.

Employment rose slightly, mostly through replacement hiring, and prices rose moderately as firms cited tariff-related expenses. Data center-related imports also rose.

Bonds rallied. The 10-year Treasury yield fell 9 basis points to 4.84%, the 2-year yield dropped 5 basis points to 4.63% and the 30-year yield declined 9 basis points to 5.23%.

Gold was flat at $3,557 an ounce, silver slipped 0.3% to $40.79 and Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) edged up 0.3% to $59,919. The CBOE Volatility Index eased to 27.6 after touching 34.95.

10 Tech Stocks Bouncing Off the Lows

The names hit hardest at the open led the recovery: AI infrastructure, memory and chip suppliers.

Read Also: 3 Things Every Bear Market in 50 Years Had in Common — Which One Is Missing Now?

Meanwhile, not everyone is buying the bounce.

“We are not out of the woods with the downside risk from the AI trade, as the Jensen Huang stock put is fading,” Chris Brigati, chief investment officer at SWBC, said in emailed comments. He expects the S&P 500 to dip close to 6,500 by year-end.

Jefferies equity strategist Steven DeSanctis sees the market’s breadth as the quieter story. “We have argued all year that we would see a broader equity market, thanks to earnings growth coming in better than average and more companies delivering over 20% earnings growth,” he said in a note Wednesday.

U.S. markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early Friday at 1 p.m. ET. A single higher low does not make a bottom, but it gives the bulls their first line in the sand.

title: Klarna Expands Global Reach With European Shopping Tool, Canadian Virtual Card Ahead Of Black Friday
desc:
Klarna Group plc (NYSE:KLAR) announced two international expansion initiatives Wednesday, expanding its price comparison tool across Europe and launching a flexible virtual card in Canada.

Separately, Wedbush analyst Moshe Katri assumed coverage on the stock with a Neutral rating and a price target of $14.

Klarna Expands Price Comparison Tool Across9 European Markets

Klarna expanded its Search & Compare tool to Switzerland, the Czech Republic, Poland, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia, Greece, Belgium and Portugal, ahead of the holiday shopping season.

Available through Klarna’s app and website, the tool enables consumers to compare product prices across thousands of retailers, including merchants outside Klarna’s existing network.

The tool enables shoppers to filter products by size, color, customer reviews, availability and delivery options.

Canadian Expansion

Klarna launched its One-Time Card in Canada, allowing consumers to access flexible payment options at nearly all online retailers accepting Visa payments online.

Previously, Canadian consumers could use Klarna’s payment services only at merchants directly integrated with its platform.

The single-use virtual prepaid card supports four interest-free installments and longer-term financing options.

Klarna launched in Canada in 2022 and in 2025 partnered with Walmart Canada to offer Klarna’s flexible payments.

The launch follows Klarna’s expanded collaboration with Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) on Monday, enabling merchants across the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and Europe to offer flexible payments without requiring separate technical integrations.

Klarna’s Recent Financial Performance

Klarna on Nov. 17 reported a third-quarter loss per share of 19 cents, wider than the analyst-estimated loss of 15 cents.

Revenue rose 12% year over year to $1.009 billion, exceeding the consensus estimate of $963.877 million.

GMV rose 10% year over year to $36.1 billion, while transaction margin dollars increased 32% to $371 million.

The company ended the quarter with 122 million active consumers, up 7%, and 1.35 million merchants, up 59%.

CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski highlighted Klarna’s fourth consecutive quarter of revenue exceeding $1 billion and positive adjusted operating income. Transaction margin increased to 37% of revenue from 31% a year earlier.

For 2026, management reaffirmed its guidance, expecting GMV of $149 billion-$151 billion and revenue of $4.08 billion-$4.16 billion. The revenue outlook compares with the analyst estimate of $4.135 billion.

Analyst Outlook

The stock carries a Hold rating with an average price forecast of $18.27 (high: $27.00; low: $13.00) across 28 analysts. Recent analyst moves include:

title: Why Is Super Micro Computer Stock Falling on Wednesday?
desc:
Super Micro Computer Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is trading lower Wednesday, extending its recent decline as a broad selloff in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks weighs on market sentiment.

The Nasdaq is down 3.82%, while the S&P 500 has fallen 2.41%, with the technology sector leading losses with a 4.7% decline.

Technology is the worst-performing sector today, ranking 11 out of 11. Over the past 30 days, the sector is down 19.58%, and over the past 90 days, it is down 20.56%, illustrating why rallies in stocks like Super Micro Computer have struggled to hold.

Read Also: Google Is Turning AI Performance Into a Price War Anthropic Can’t Ignore

Rate Hike Projections Weigh

Broader market weakness adds pressure as growing expectations of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes weigh on technology and AI stocks.

Projections from the CME Group’s FedWatch tool show markets pricing in a 99.8% likelihood of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates after its December meeting.

Sector Volatility and Supply

Earlier this week, Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) drove Wall Street sentiment when its stock gained 31.5% on Monday after the company reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, sparking a relief rally across AI and semiconductor stocks.

title: Why is Microcap NeuroSense Therapeutics Stock Rallying on Wednesday?
desc:
NeuraLight announced Monday that its proprietary biomarker platform detected a statistically significant slowdown in brain function deterioration among amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) patients receiving NeuroSense Therapeutics Ltd.‘s (NASDAQ:NRSN) investigational therapy, PrimeC.

The results come from the Phase 2b PARADIGM trial, where NeuraLight’s precision brain function biomarkers measured clear separation between patients taking PrimeC and those on a placebo.

Read Also: Novartis Halts Experimental ALS Drug Trial but Acquires Brain Delivery Platform

Measuring Treatment Efficacy in Short-Duration Trials

Patients treated with PrimeC experienced significantly slower brain function decline compared to the placebo group after just six months of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase, showing an 85% effect size (p=0.04).

The gap between the original treatment groups widened further during the subsequent open-label extension.

These outcomes occurred within a brief six-month timeframe and a small sub-cohort of 36 ALS patients.

The data highlight the sensitivity of NeuraLight’s platform in capturing treatment-driven changes in brain function despite limited sample sizes.

Aligning Objective Readouts With Clinical Data

The biomarker findings offer an independent, objective functional readout that supports previously reported clinical and biological data from the PARADIGM study.

Earlier data published in JAMA Neurology showed that PrimeC slowed functional decline while modulating biological biomarkers tied to the disease.

Tracking brain function changes remains a primary obstacle in developing drugs for neurodegenerative conditions, especially during brief trials with small patient groups.

AI-Driven Eye-Movement Analysis

NeuraLight addresses this challenge through an AI-powered platform that extracts quantitative brain function biomarkers from eye-movement measurements.

By combining neuroscience with proprietary data and artificial intelligence, the healthtech company enables pharmaceutical developers to monitor neural pathways at scale.

The alignment of clinical results, biological biomarkers, and objective brain function measurements in the PARADIGM trial demonstrates how NeuraLight’s technology helps drugmakers prove that a therapy’s biological activity preserves measurable brain function.

title: Analog Devices Analyst Cuts Forecast on Sector Valuation Reset
desc:
Analog Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:ADI) delivered stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Tuesday. However, higher operating expenses weighed on its earnings outlook.

Needham Maintains Buy, Cuts Price Forecast

Needham analyst N. Quinn Bolton maintained a Buy rating on Analog Devices but reduced his 12-month price forecast from $450 to $400, citing lower valuation multiples across the semiconductor sector.

Bolton expects capacity expansion, strong demand for industrial products and continued data center growth to support above-seasonal revenue growth in fiscal 2027.

He raised his fiscal 2027 revenue forecast to $18.75 billion from $17.95 billion.

Quarterly Earnings Beat Estimates

Analog Devices reported fourth-quarter revenue of $4.373 billion, up 42.2% year over year and 8.7% sequentially, exceeding Wall Street’s $4.320 billion estimate.

Adjusted earnings reached $4.06 per share, beating the $3.89 consensus by 17 cents.

Adjusted gross margin reached 74.5%, surpassing the 74% estimate, while operating expenses totaled $971.9 million.

Industrial And Automotive Drive Growth

Industrial revenue jumped 54.6% year over year to $2.194 billion, supported by demand for AI infrastructure, aerospace, defense and automated test equipment.

Automotive revenue increased 20.7% to $1.044 billion, reflecting demand for connectivity, audio processing and battery management systems.

Communications revenue surged 80.8% to $706.8 million but missed Needham’s $720 million estimate.

Consumer revenue climbed 7.1% to $429.4 million, exceeding expectations despite memory-related headwinds.

Data Center Demand Supports Outlook

Bolton highlighted more than 100% year-over-year data center revenue growth in the fourth quarter and over 90% growth for fiscal 2026.

Optical products outpaced power products during the quarter, although both contributed to expansion.

He expects continued growth across both categories in fiscal 2027.

Data center bookings exceeded billings, which Bolton viewed as evidence of underlying customer demand rather than inventory restocking.

Outside aerospace and defense, automated test equipment and data centers, the broader product portfolio showed no significant signs of restocking.

Gross Margins And Capacity Expansion

Needham expects first-quarter fiscal 2027 gross margin to moderate to approximately 74%, reflecting seasonal factory shutdowns.

Bolton expects revenue growth and a favorable industrial product mix, rather than increased factory utilization, to drive subsequent margin improvement.

He raised his fiscal 2027 gross margin forecast to 74.4% from 74%.

Analog Devices plans to invest approximately $1.6 billion–$1.9 billion in fiscal 2027 capital expenditures, primarily expanding U.S. and European fabrication facilities and testing and assembly capacity.

Management expects new fabrication capacity to become available in stages beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2028.

First-Quarter Guidance Signals Higher Costs

Analog Devices forecasts first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $4.4 billion, above Wall Street’s $4.356 billion estimate.

However, its adjusted EPS guidance of $3.82 fell below the $3.88 consensus, reflecting higher expected operating expenses of approximately $1.035 billion.

Management expects sequential growth in industrial and communications revenue, while automotive revenue may decline slightly and consumer sales could fall 10%–15%.

Bolton expects operating expenses to grow at approximately half the pace of revenue throughout fiscal 2027, supporting profitability as capacity expansion and product demand strengthen.

title: The Rich Got Into SpaceX Early. Brian Armstrong Wants to Change That
desc:
Why should wealth determine who gets access to investment opportunities at earlier, potentially cheaper valuations?

Coinbase Global Inc. (NASDAQ:COIN) CEO Brian Armstrong recently addressed that question in a Nov. 24 post on X. The 43-year-old billionaire pointed out how the biggest stock-market debuts of 2026 expose a divide. By the time some of the world’s most valuable private companies reach public markets, much of their early wealth creation has already happened.

Want to Invest? Pass a Test

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX), Anthropic, PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) and SK hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY) — the year’s mega-listings — benefited companies and a small group of private investors, Armstron explained. However, the IPOs were less favorable for average investors.

An overhaul of accredited-investor rules is worth considering, he explained. His solution? People must pass a financial-literacy test to qualify for private-market access instead of relying on wealth or income.

The IPO Windfall Starts Before Listing

SpaceX raised about $75 billion in its June U.S. offering. Anthropic raised about $81.3 billion in November. Together, the deals accounted for roughly 80% of the $195.6 billion raised by 53 U.S. IPOs valued at $1 billion or more through Nov. 19, according to Stock Titan’s tally of SEC filings.

But access to an IPO is not the same as access to the private funding rounds that came before it. Early investors may have bought shares at valuations far below the public offering price, capturing gains later buyers cannot replicate simply by purchasing on the first day of trading.

SK hynix, also cited by Armstrong, was already publicly listed in South Korea; its 2026 U.S. listing was an American depositary share offering, not a conventional IPO.

Read Also: SpaceX Stock: Musk's Giveaway Meets Insider Sales

Armstrong’s Proposal Lands as Regulators Consider Similar Route

On Sept. 30, the Securities and Exchange Commission sought public comment on whether passing an accredited-investor exam developed by FINRA could become an additional way for individuals to qualify.

The exam could test knowledge of securities, investing, and financial and business matters, offering a non-financial way to demonstrate sophistication.

That is not an adopted rule, and the SEC’s request is narrower than opening private markets to anyone who passes a test. Accredited-investor standards exist partly because private offerings can carry less disclosure, less liquidity and greater risk than publicly traded stocks. A test might broaden access, but it would not remove those risks or guarantee investors can absorb losses.

Investment Takeaway

The debate is whether financial knowledge can serve as a better gatekeeper than wealth. Investors should watch the SEC’s comment process, which runs through Dec. 4, and whether regulators advance an exam-based pathway.

For Coinbase, Armstrong’s intervention reinforces a broader ambition to make financial markets more accessible — but the policy outcome, and any commercial benefit to COIN, remain uncertain.

title: Bitcoin Faces the ‘Worst Combination for Crypto’ as Rates and Dollar Stay High

title: Bristol Myers Squibb Reports Split Data in Lupus Studies
desc:
Bristol Myers Squibb & Co. (NYSE:BMY) on Wednesday shared topline results from POETYK SLE-1 and POETYK SLE-2, two pivotal Phase 3 trials evaluating the efficacy and safety of Sotyktu (deucravacitinib) for moderate-to-severe systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

SLE, commonly known as lupus, is a chronic autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks healthy tissues and organs throughout the body.

It affects roughly 3.4 million people worldwide and typically alternates between periods of worsening symptoms (flares) and periods of little to no symptoms (remission).

Read Also: Johnson & Johnson Touts Encouraging Results For Experimental Lupus Treatment

POETYK SLE-1 Trial Meets Primary and Key Secondary Endpoints

The POETYK SLE-1 trial met the primary endpoint, with a significantly greater proportion of patients treated with Sotyktu achieving a Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Responder Index-4 (SRI-4) response, a composite measure of disease activity, at Week 52 compared with placebo.

Additionally, Sotyktu demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements across multiple measures of SLE disease activity, with statistically significant effects on the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group-based Composite Lupus Assessment (BICLA), SRI-4 with steroid taper and patient-reported fatigue.

Responses for all other key secondary endpoints were numerically greater for Sotyktu but were not statistically significant.

High Placebo Response Impacts POETYK SLE-2 Primary Endpoint

In the POETYK SLE-2 trial, Sotyktu demonstrated a level of response consistent with POETYK SLE-1; however, the primary endpoint was not met due to a higher placebo response than was seen in POETYK SLE-1.

Notably, numerical improvements were observed for Sotyktu compared with placebo across all key secondary endpoints in POETYK SLE-2.

Sotyktu Safety Profile Remains Consistent Across Both Lupus Trials

Sotyktu demonstrated a well-tolerated safety profile across both the POETYK SLE-1 and POETYK SLE-2 trials, consistent with the established safety profile in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. In both trials, discontinuations due to adverse events were low.

Regulatory Next Steps and Ongoing Sjögren’s Disease Trial

The company will complete a comprehensive evaluation of the SLE clinical trial data, including data from both the Phase 2 and Phase 3 studies, and engage with health authorities.

As part of its broader strategy in rheumatic diseases, Bristol Myers Squibb is also evaluating Sotyktu in the ongoing Phase 3 POETYK clinical trial in Sjögren’s disease, with results expected in 2027.

BMY Price Action: Bristol-Myers Squibb shares were down 1.18% at $61.29 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: You'll Never Believe What 'Uranium One' Hillary Clinton Said About Nvidia Scandal
desc:
You'll Never Believe What 'Uranium One' Hillary Clinton Said About Nvidia Scandal

Hillary Clinton wants Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang called "Supergate."

"Is it a national security scandal? Yes," Clinton wrote on X on Monday, hours after Nvidia's board put Huang back in charge at President Trump's urging. "Is it a corruption scandal? Yes. Is it an insider trading scandal? Yes. Is it a market manipulation scandal? Yes."

Is it a national security scandal? Yes.

Is it a corruption scandal? Yes.

Is it an insider trading scandal? Yes.

Is it a market manipulation scandal? Yes.

If it's "super intelligence," call it Supergate.

— Hillary Clinton (@HillaryClinton) November 23, 2026

Of course - Clinton is uniquely qualified to spot a national-security and corruption scandal. As Secretary of State she sat on the CFIUS panel that approved the sale of Uranium One - owner of roughly 20% of US uranium production capacity - to Rosatom, Russia's state atomic-energy company. In the same period the Clinton Foundation and related entities took millions from Uranium One investors and other parties with a stake in the deal; Bill Clinton separately collected a $500,000 speaking fee from a Russian bank. The arrangement has never been fully investigated. She has also never been charged for the private server that, according to the FBI, handled 110 emails in 52 chains containing classified information, eight of those chains Top Secret. The same pattern appears in the Clinton Foundation's foreign-government donations while she ran the State Department and in the cattle-futures windfall that turned $1,000 into nearly $100,000 under the guidance of a Tyson Foods lawyer. None of it has stopped her from labeling the Nvidia board's decision a national-security, corruption, insider-trading, and market-manipulation scandal.

Piers Morgan read the post out on Wednesday's Piers Morgan Uncensored, introducing Clinton as someone "who knows a thing or two about scandals," and then laid out the case the newly elected Democrats will bring when they arrive in Washington in January. "An adulterous billionaire tech boss might have allowed a Chinese spying mistress to hand China an edge in the existential AI race," Morgan said. "They're going to have a field day. And frankly, it would be gross negligence if they didn't."

The spy half of that case has wobbled since the Wall Street Journal reported late Monday that US intelligence has no smoking gun on Alice Huang and that her links to Chinese intelligence may be only circumstantial, three weeks after the paper reported that officials in the US, Singapore and Taiwan feared she was a Chinese intelligence source.

Morgan then played Fox News host Jesse Watters, who sees it ending the same way. "The Democrats will likely use this scandal to impeach," Watters said. "They will say the president is manipulating the market to enrich himself and his cabinet." He added: "And a bunch of Republicans in Congress aren't going to defend him. So this is going to get ugly fast."

In the release announcing Huang's return, the board said it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and, based on that input, is "confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk," according to the company's 8-K. "So in a nutshell, the president and his team told us there is nothing to see here," Morgan said.

Clinton knows the first charge on her list from the other side. In July 2016 the FBI concluded that she and her aides had been "extremely careless in their handling of very sensitive, highly classified information" on the private email server she used as secretary of state: 110 emails in 52 chains held information that was classified when sent or received, eight of the chains at Top Secret. Then-Director James Comey recommended no charges.

Clinton herself turned $1,000 into nearly $100,000 trading cattle futures in 1978 and 1979, guided by James Blair, a friend and a top lawyer for Tyson Foods, while her husband went from Arkansas attorney general to governor. The White House put her net gain at $26,521 for 1978 and $72,996 for 1979 when the trades came out in 1994. She was never charged.

None of that kept Joe Biden from awarding her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in January 2025. Now she is calling Trump's Nvidia rescue an insider trading scandal.

title: Houthis Target Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Port Of Jeddah For First Time Ever
desc:
Houthis Target Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Port Of Jeddah For First Time Ever

Via The Cradle

The Yemeni Armed Forces (YAF/Houthis) announced on Wednesday its first operation targeting the Saudi port of Jeddah, in response to the kingdom’s recent airstrikes on Hodeidah Port.

The YAF also announced a second operation targeting the Saudi port of Jizan, "as part of the response to the Saudi aggression against our country, and in retaliation for its targeting of the port of Hodeidah, and in order to establish the equation of port for port."

Both attacks were “accurate” and “resulted in damage to the targeted sites,” the YAF added. It stressed that it “will not hesitate to respond directly and immediately to any aggression targeting the port of Hodeidah” and “will continue to establish deterrence equations, whatever the consequences and repercussions.”

Both facilities are vital to the kingdom and are situated on Saudi Arabia’s western Red Sea coast. The Saudi-led coalition claimed it intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by the Yemeni army near Jeddah Islamic Port, but acknowledged that a projectile struck the port of Jizan. It said the strike caused minor damage.

Unverified videos on social media allegedly showed fires breaking out at the Jeddah facility. This was the first YAF operation ever targeting the Saudi port of Jeddah.

The kingdom launched a heavy attack on the western Yemeni port of Hodeidah early on 25 November. Attacks also targeted Sanaa International Airport. The Yemeni army (Houthis) had warned earlier that all Saudi ports would become targets if Hodeidah Port came under renewed aggression.

Since the kingdom’s escalation of its decade-long war on Yemen in July, oil refineries, energy storage sites, military bases, and airports across Saudi Arabia have been targeted.

The YAF has heavily targeted Saudi energy infrastructure across the kingdom and has launched multiple attacks on the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, targeting refineries and energy facilities operated by Riyadh.

Sanaa has vowed to continue its operations against sites within Saudi Arabia, as well as its advance on the ground inside Yemen, which recently saw its forces seize Bab al-Mandab from the kingdom’s proxies.

The Yemeni army (Houthis) now controls the entire western coast of the country, giving it increased leverage over Saudi and Israeli shipping in the Red Sea.

Riyadh is preparing for its war against Yemen to “stretch well into next year,” despite the setbacks it has faced in the conflict, two western officials were cited by Reuters as saying on 18 November. Over 450 people have been killed in Yemen by the Saudi-led coalition since July 2026, according to the Yemeni Health Ministry.

title: Georgia Voters To Decide Fate Of Massive $17 Billion Data Center After Furious Residents Revolt
desc:
Georgia Voters To Decide Fate Of Massive $17 Billion Data Center After Furious Residents Revolt

Coweta County voters will decide in a Jan. 12 special election whether to repeal the rezoning for Project Sail, a $17 billion data center campus on more than 800 rural acres about 45 miles southwest of Atlanta that county commissioners approved 3-2 in April.

Probate Judge Carrie B. Markham ordered the election Monday. Opponents filed their petition Oct. 16 under the Home Rule provision of the Georgia Constitution, which let them force a vote with signatures from 10% of the county's electorate: 10,971 names, out of 109,703 active electors in the last general election, according to Markham's Nov. 23 order. Organizers turned in 14,820 signatures, and the county's director of elections verified 11,065 of them, clearing the bar by 94.

The ballot question reaches well past one project: besides repealing the April 7 rezoning, it would strip data centers from the county's zoning code and ban data centers and cryptocurrency mining operations in every zoning district in Coweta County. The order puts it to voters this way:

"Shall the action of the Coweta County Board of Commissioners on April 7, 2026 approving REZONE 24-019 be repealed, and Appendix A. Zoning and Development of the Coweta County Code of Ordinances be amended to delete data centers and data center campuses as permitted and conditional uses in all zoning districts and to prohibit data centers, data center campuses, cryptocurrency data centers, and cryptocurrency mining operations in all zoning districts of Coweta County?"

Atlas Development, the Buford-based company that filed the rezoning, objected to the petition on Oct. 23. Markham threw the objection out in a separate order the same day she called the election, finding that under Georgia Supreme Court precedent no party has legal standing to object to a petition filed under the Home Rule provision, and that Atlas's objection wasn't verified in any case.

The state's high court opened that door last year in a fight over Hogg Hummock, the Gullah Geechee community on Sapelo Island, when it ruled unanimously that a McIntosh County zoning ordinance was subject to the same referendum procedure Coweta's opponents used.

"The County became aware of this news at the same time as our citizens," Coweta's communications manager, Cathy Wickey, said in a statement. "Given the unique nature of this situation, we are still assessing its potential implications. We anticipate that legal questions and challenges may arise among the entities involved." The county will pay for the election, run it on its normal equipment and precincts, and the court will certify the result, according to the order.

Prologis, the San Francisco-based industrial REIT under contract to take over the project, said in October, when the petition's signatures came in, that the petition "does not change our commitment to Project Sail." Its executive JC Witt said in April that the site was chosen partly for its closeness to Georgia Power's Plant Yates, and that "the question isn't if this site will be developed. It's just how."

Atlas's filings with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs describe 13 buildings of about 378,000 square feet each, plus substations, finished by the end of 2036 and worth $17,161,900,000 at build-out. The same filings put its water demand at 9.1 million gallons a day, with 3.03 million gallons a day of sewage and 800 tons of solid waste a year. Prologis has pitched a smaller version, nine buildings and about 4.3 million square feet drawing roughly 900 megawatts.

The tax windfall that sold the project has shrunk: Atlas first projected more than $1 billion a year in local taxes, a figure the Atlanta Journal-Constitution found was erroneous; Prologis's latest projection is about $100 million a year, while the state filings list $163 million.

Commissioners Alphonso Smith, Jeff Fisher and John Reidelbach voted for the rezoning, which moved about 829 acres near Sargent and Wagers Mill roads from Rural Conservation to Industrial. "This is a no-brainer for the county," Smith said at the time. A group of residents sued in May in Coweta County Superior Court to void it, alleging that commissioners ignored the land's conservation designation and its role in groundwater recharge; that case is pending.

Yard signs against the project line home after home along Wagers Mill Road in Newnan. "The voters should have the right to decide," resident Leroy Kenner told Atlanta News First.

"We are thrilled with the Judge's order," Vivian Allen, a volunteer with Citizens for Rural Coweta, said in a release. "Thousands of our neighbors signed because they wanted a say, and we can't wait to see Coweta County turn out on January 12." Fellow volunteer Donna Boles credited the canvassers: "This happened because people stood in parking lots, on sidewalks, and at local events collecting signatures in the summer heat. This vote belongs to them."

Coweta has been on the front line of Georgia's data center build-out for months: Georgia Power is seizing homes and easements across Coweta and Fayette counties for a 35-mile, 500-kilovolt line to feed AI data centers. And when voters elsewhere got a direct say this month, 41 local measures in ten states went almost unanimously against the data centers.

If Coweta's measure passes on Jan. 12, it won't stop at Project Sail: no data center or crypto mine could be zoned anywhere in the county.

title: Judge Upholds NYC Rent Freeze, Siding With "Reckless And Irresponsible" Mamdani Over Landlords
desc:
Judge Upholds NYC Rent Freeze, Siding With "Reckless And Irresponsible" Mamdani Over Landlords

Authored by Jacki Thrapp via The Epoch Times,

Manhattan Supreme Court Judge Brendan Lantry on Wednesday tossed out a challenge to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's rent freeze on one- and two-year leases.

The freeze, which applies to tenants living in around 1 million New York City apartments, was challenged by owners of housing units after Mamdani's hand-picked Rent Guidelines Board voted for it 7-1 in June.

The vote aligned with one of Mamdani's central campaign promises, which Lantry called "reckless and irresponsible" in the order released on Nov. 25.

"The Mayor of the City of New York has no authority to unilaterally raise, 'freeze' or otherwise adjust the rent of stabilized units in this City - that responsibility is within the power of the Board and the Board alone," Lantry wrote.

However, Lantry said that the petitioners - the landlords - "failed to establish that the passing of Order No. 58 was unreasonable, arbitrary, or capricious."

Ann Korchak, the board president of Small Property Owners of New York (SPONY), called the ruling "terribly disappointing to small property owners."

"The courts have become our only recourse against the destructive, politically-driven housing regulations and laws that are plunging small rent-stabilized buildings into severe economic distress," Korchak wrote in a statement to The Epoch Times on Wednesday.

SPONY represents some plaintiffs in the lawsuit.

"The rent freeze will push more small rent-stabilized property owners to the edge of the cliff," Korchak added. "It denies the resources they need to maintain and operate their rent-stabilized buildings. Property taxes, water and sewer rates, and insurance, energy, heating, repair and other costs and expenses aren't frozen. Rents should not be frozen, either."

The Epoch Times reached out to the mayor's office and the Rent Guidelines Board for comment.

The average price to rent an apartment in New York City is $3,550, according to data by Zillow on Nov. 23.

The citywide average monthly collected rent in buildings containing rent-stabilized units was $1,681, according to the New York City Rent Guidelines Board's 2026 Income and Expense Study.

Rents varied significantly by building age.

Units in pre-1974 buildings averaged $1,521 per month, while those in post-1973 buildings averaged $2,374.

Manhattan had the highest average among the boroughs at $2,295 per month. Brooklyn and Queens both averaged roughly $1,600 to $1,700, while the Bronx and Staten Island came in below $1,200.

The board decided to freeze rents after a review of wages, inflation, maintenance costs, taxes, and landlord incomes.

Tenants supported a freeze or outright reduction at public hearings before the vote, citing stagnant pay and higher living costs.

Property owners and their representatives said it would hurt landlords with building upkeep and mortgage payments.

title: Listen: LaGuardia Pilot Asks What A 'MANPADS Alert' Means As Tower Warns Of Missile Sighting
desc:
Listen: LaGuardia Pilot Asks What A 'MANPADS Alert' Means As Tower Warns Of Missile Sighting

Air traffic controllers at New York's LaGuardia Airport warned pilots of a reported man-portable air-defense system (MANPADS) sighting just east of the airport around 6:30 p.m. ET on Wednesday, the night before Thanksgiving. The report was deemed not credible within the half hour, according to Breaking911.

The air traffic control tower at New York's Laguardia Airport REUTERS/Ryan Murphy (via wabcradio.com)

"Attention aircraft, MANPADS alert, just east of LaGuardia," the tower broadcast, asking every crew on the frequency for its intentions.

BREAKING: LaGuardia Airport's control tower issued another alert about a man-portable air-defense system (MANPADS) sighting just east of the airport around 6:30 p.m. ET. pic.twitter.com/meRrzG7Me6

— Breaking911 (@Breaking911) November 25, 2026

One crew was told to "exercise extreme caution," and American 407 was told to keep holding in position.

"We're going to hold right here," came the reply.

"I have no idea what a MANPADS alert means. I was in the Navy, I know what MANPADS means, but I don't know if that's what it means."

The controller spelled it out: a man-portable air defense system, the shoulder-fired missiles built to bring down low-flying aircraft.

A member of the Venezuelan military holds a 9K338 Igla-S MANPADS launcher in Caracas on October 30, 2025. Photo by Federico PARRA / AFP FEDERICO PARRA (Photo by Federico PARRA / AFP FEDERICO PARRA)

UPDATE: The MANPADS report near LaGuardia Airport has been deemed not credible. https://t.co/LlQoN9WeBF

— Breaking911 (@Breaking911) November 25, 2026

It is the second time since July that LaGuardia's tower has put inbound pilots on alert for a shoulder-fired missile. On July 21, controllers told a Delta Air Lines pilot on approach to "use extreme caution" after a report of a man with a rocket launcher near Terminal C. Port Authority police searched the airport and found the threat unfounded, CBS News reported.

"Use extreme caution": A Delta Air Lines pilot approaching New York's LaGuardia Airport was warned by air traffic control Tuesday to be on the lookout for a possible man-portable air defense system, or MANPADS, following a reported threat. The Port Authority said police searched... pic.twitter.com/RnzGbtm4Qk

— CBS News (@CBSNews) July 22, 2026

Wednesday's alert landed in the middle of the Thanksgiving getaway, with flyers already heading into storms on both coasts.

title: "Causing Sheer Chaos": Nvidia Halts AI Chip Shipments To Four Southeast Asian Countries
desc:
"Causing Sheer Chaos": Nvidia Halts AI Chip Shipments To Four Southeast Asian Countries

Nvidia has told top manufacturing partners to halt server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries as tighter US export controls threaten a data center boom fueled by Chinese demand for AI computing power.

The Financial Times reports that Dell and Supermicro are among the suppliers that have told customers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia that their orders can no longer be shipped. The report cites three people familiar with the matter.

In other words, the Southeast Asian back door into Chinese AI compute just slammed shut, and the people who financed the door are now trying to sell it.

As a reminder, the Chinese hyperscalers, which could no longer buy Blackwells, had simply been renting them from data centers in Southeast Asia. That workaround is now frozen, and with it the financing that was built on the assumption that ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent would be the long-term tenants.

Goldman's European industrials desk is hearing the same thing from the other end of the supply chain. Jeremy Elster wrote this morning that investor sentiment is "moving into acceptance mode as the reasons for further potential weakness are becoming visible", and spelled out what that means:

In a nutshell, it is now base case that we will see some sort of dacatentre order "air pocket" for a period in 2027.

It remains unclear whether the suspension is temporary while Nvidia and its partners determine how to comply.

The US Commerce Department's new rules give cloud providers 90 days to obtain licenses by demonstrating that their end customers do not include restricted entities, including those in China.

"There's this new rule but no guidance on execution," said a cloud provider executive.

"No one knows how to apply for this license while the 90-day clock is ticking. It's causing sheer chaos in the region."

Last week, a $480 million loan for Singapore-based Aolani Cloud Pte to fund Nvidia AI chips intended to serve ByteDance was put on hold amid compliance uncertainty.

Among the largest transactions under review is a $6.6 billion loan for Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centers, whose Malaysian facilities serve customers including ByteDance, according to a separate Bloomberg report.

Other financing deals facing disruption in Southeast Asia include:

  • Digital Halo: One bank passed on a fully underwritten $372 million loan for a Malaysian data center serving Alibaba and other customers.
  • GMI Cloud: At least one private fund declined to participate in a $300 million loan to finance chips for a Thai data center intended to serve Tencent.

Notably, Asia-Pacific data-center loans have jumped from basically zero to $49 billion in just several years, according to Bloomberg data.

The latest restrictions threaten to slow that expansion and could redirect computing capacity originally intended for Southeast Asia toward the US market.

And that is where it gets interesting. Chips that were already racked and running for Chinese remote customers have nowhere to go, so they are being sold:

At the same time, an unusually high volume of already-deployed advanced GPUs (notably B300 systems with full HBM) has appeared on the secondary market since the rule, consistent with the CNBC/DigiTimes coverage of chips coming up for sale as SE Asia operators remarket capacity to reduce exposure. This creates a temporary chip glut as facilities originally allocated for Chinese remote offtake are pushed toward Western buyers, offering near-term incremental supply that hyperscalers and neoclouds can absorb.

And that might already be playing out, as we discuss in the note titled The GPU Landlord Blinks? SpaceX Reportedly Slashes Blackwell Rents As Anthropic Hands Back 50,000 H200S.

And while the equity market can't decide whether the glut is temporary, the credit market has made up its mind about who is most exposed:

CoreWeave five-year CDS is around 1,314bp, implying roughly a 68% probability of default over five years, while its bonds yield close to 18%. Oracle’s five-year CDS is around 356bp and SoftBank’s is 501bp, with record CDS levels at Oracle and Alphabet suggesting concerns are spreading to higher-quality names.

Read that again: the market is pricing better-than-even odds that the poster child of the neocloud model, CoreWeave (CRWV), defaults within five years, at the same time that a flood of used GPUs is hitting the market and at least one big GPU landlord is reportedly slashing spot rates.

And the contagion is no longer confined to the levered renters; Oracle (ORCL) and Alphabet (GOOGL) protection is at record levels.

We give the last word to Goldman tech trader Peter Bartlett with a line that every AI bull should tape to their monitor: with the year-end catalysts already spent, "the question is now are we waiting for estimate CUTS before Semis / AI-Infra can bottom?"
